# AI借款人競逐資金，美債長端殖利率再創高點

## 升息預期延後，仍保護不了長債

即使市場將Fed下次升息預期推至1月，30年期美債殖利率仍上升6個基點至5.31%，創2007年以來最高。10年期上升4個基點至4.72%，2年與5年期各升2個基點至4.19%及4.38%。曲線再度轉陡，2年與10年期利差擴大2個基點至53個基點，2年與30年期擴大4個基點至112個基點。

6月美伊備忘錄到期，雙方仍未達成持久協議，川普也表示無意延長，油價因而增加壓力。WTI上漲3.05%至$84.91，布蘭特上漲2.94%至$91.12。不過，10年期損益兩平通膨率僅升1個基點至2.28%，實質殖利率則升3個基點至2.44%。政府借款與AI投資競逐長期儲蓄，投資人要求提高的主要是扣除通膨後的報酬。

8月投資級發行額創紀錄、達$1,452億。Blackstone Private Credit Fund與Blue Owl Technology Finance增額發行，Alphabet則開始行銷澳幣債。借款人持續取得資金，長存續期間資產卻較受傷：LQD下跌0.40%，HYG與JNK各跌約0.13%，20年以上美國公債指數跌0.77%。Sammons Financial另因關係人疑慮利差擴大，屬個別發行人的衝擊。

其他資產表現不一。S&P 500下跌0.52%，Nasdaq 100跌0.17%，半導體卻漲1.64%。美元指數下跌0.13%至99.54，黃金期貨上漲2.25%至$4,479.10。AI獲利樂觀與Fed升息延後，仍不足以讓每項資產免於長期資金變貴的影響。

海外方面，日本GDP疲弱仍未阻止10年期日債殖利率升至2.93%、創1996年以來最高。印度意外縮短美元存款優惠方案，減少預期中的盧比流動性，短債受創較深；希臘則計畫提前還債以降低未來供給。各國決策不同，也不能因Fed可以再等，就假設海外債券都會上漲。

## 公司長債抵銷部分美債供給減輕的效果

30年期收盤高於前一週5.216%的得標利率，10年期也高於自身4.683%的標售水準。標售需求足夠，卻未替殖利率設下持久上限。近一個月2年期僅高1個基點，10年與30年期卻分別高17及25個基點。30年期實質殖利率週一上升6個基點至3.06%，與名目升幅相同；市場對下一次升息25個基點的預期，則從一週前的12月延至1月。

供給數字有助解釋，為何美債發行減輕仍未讓長債喘息。聯邦年度赤字接近$2兆，更依賴國庫券融資，10年與30年期標售規模維持不變。巴克萊估計，今年民間投資人須承接的附息公債淨供給約$1.2兆，比2025年少$4,400億；公司債淨供給卻預計增加$4,740億，主要來自科技業。政府債務減少的部分，正被另一種長期負債補上。

今年投資級發行接近$1.5兆，年增36%。最大型科技公司借款約$2,000億，相當於財政部對民間投資人附息債淨發行的25%，比2025年占比高五倍。10年以上債券占投資級發行約20%，去年僅13%。額外增加的$1,900億長天期公司債，接近全年$2,760億30年期美債供給的70%。

相近存續期間、較高殖利率，可能讓基金從公債轉向公司債。Alphabet近期30年期債殖利率近6.4%，較美債高約115個基點；Meta相關資料中心債則超過7.5%。Morningstar數據顯示，美國投資級債券基金將公司債配置提高至三年高點30%，同時降低美債持有。美銀經濟學家估計，公司債與房貸擔保證券供給增加，今年為10年期殖利率添了約30個基點。這是模型估計，不是週一變動的實際拆解，但方向與供給及配置變化一致。

8月$1,452億總額超過2020年的$1,360億紀錄。今年迄今$1.46兆發行，也比2020年同期高8.5%。Alphabet的$250億美元債領銜本月，亦為2026年第八筆至少這個規模的交易，全部來自科技公司。摩根大通將TMT年度預測提高約20%至$5,400億，提供後續行事曆的背景；美國勞動節後通常又會加速發行。

Alphabet目前行銷首次澳幣債，四個年期包含20年期，目標約A$50億、或$36億。此前已發行美元、瑞郎、英鎊、歐元、加幣及日圓債，上月並將2026年資本支出預測提高至最高$2,050億。澳洲境外借款人發行創紀錄，加上本地科技曝險選擇有限，可能支持需求；但這也表示公司進入另一個儲蓄市場，而非把融資需求留在美國信用市場內。

油價是另一項風險，卻不是實質殖利率上升的全部解釋。儘管船隻遭攻擊，隱蔽轉運仍讓中東生產商將大量原油移至阿曼灣，緩和相較完全中斷的衝擊。同時，黎巴嫩戰事再起、備忘錄到期，美國海軍封鎖也沒有解決時間表。若替代油流失效，通膨補償面臨的壓力可能比週一小幅上升所呈現的更大。

## 私人信貸業者增額發債，保險公司疑慮則推寬利差

Blackstone Private Credit Fund原擬籌約$5億，因訂單高峰近$20億，最後發行$7.5億5年期票據。Blue Owl Technology Finance對6月券增發$4億，為最低目標兩倍，需求約$10.5億。Blue Owl利差定在250個基點，低於既有券的265個基點；Blackstone為205個基點，較初步討論收窄約25個基點。

第二季業績減輕了市場先前對部分私人信貸軟體曝險與贖回限制的擔憂，週一交易顯示仍能以投資級條件融資。不過，前一週平均36%的訂單流失也提醒，價格收緊後初始簿冊可能縮水。強勁需求與價格紀律可以同時存在。

QTS在喬治亞州、與微軟相關的Project Odyssey融資，因需求超過$80億，可能擴至$39億。5年期債預計取得投資級評等，但6%後段票息加上折價發行，將使殖利率落在7%前段至中段，接近B級債務。租約與微軟關聯支持架構，投資人仍要求施工、專案及租戶集中風險的補償。4月QTS已為微軟算力籌得$46億，訂單高峰$125億；本次條件仍在行銷中，尚未完成定價。

Sammons Financial的2036年6月到期債券利差，由一週前147個基點擴大至約200個基點，為發行以來最弱。報導聚焦其與Guggenheim Partners的關係，引用文件中將Sammons列為關係人、並承認可能造成利益衝突的誘因。Hunterbrook Media揭露其投資關係企業持有債券空頭。惠譽6月給予A-，指出資本非常強健，但風險資產曝險略高。

Sammons曾是Guggenheim最大股東，Guggenheim則替保險公司管理數百億美元。美國檢察官及監管單位正在調查，與Mark Walter相關的保險公司是否將貸款導向其商業版圖其他部分。Guggenheim的2031年11月第一順位擔保貸款，週一報價低於面額80%，7月20日約在面額。調查與價格下跌使持股、控制權及關係人放款成為焦點，但不代表不當行為已獲證實。

## 日本GDP疲弱，卻受匯率限制牽制

日本第二季經濟年化成長1.1%，低於市場共識2%，也比第一季修正後1.9%慢。雖已連續第三季擴張，民間消費卻持平，不如預期增加0.4%；資本投資非年化季減1.2%，前季修正為減1%，本次原預期增0.5%。單看內需，急於緊縮的理由不強。

日債仍然下跌。10年期殖利率最多升5.5個基點至2.93%，20年期升6.5個基點至3.815%，30年期升6個基點至4.07%，接近5月紀錄。隔夜交換反映9月18日升息機率約80%。產出弱可能降低連續升息的預期，卻未移除下一次升息的理由。

日圓約每美元159，遠弱於十年平均126.09，也僅部分收復7月163.99的四十年低點。7月底協同干預減緩跌勢，卻未消除利差。高市政府支持近期升息，可能在9月或10月，植田也在7月維持1%利率後強調通膨上行風險。穩定匯率在緊縮論述中的分量愈來愈重。

前財務省高階匯率官員中尾武彥主張每次會議升息，將利率拉到2%以上；他認為通膨約2%時，2.25%或2.5%並不異常，並提及利差與日本$1.2兆外匯存底仍提供干預能力。他不是現任決策者，這些意見擴大的是公共討論範圍，而非官方承諾。

7月企業物價年增7.2%，仍促使公司轉嫁燃料與原料成本。荷莫茲實質關閉之際，美國占日本6月石油進口近三分之一，2月僅7%。年度加薪及公用事業補貼可能支持消費，但薪資與資產收益較少的家庭，仍承受生活成本。高市已限制公用事業費率，並計畫自4月起兩年將食品消費稅降至1%，尚無明確財源，公共債務卻已超過全年產出兩倍。

更廣泛的債市也遠非同步寬鬆。32個交換市場中，三分之二反映升息，七個主要市場未來一年合計約400個基點。韓國以超過100個基點居首，其公債今年本幣報酬近負9%，日本約負4%。法國10年期近期升至2009年以來最高，德國與義大利殖利率今年已升逾30個基點。

中國形成對照。7月工業生產年增率降至4.5%，零售增速降至0.6%，前七個月固定資產投資下降6.7%，城鎮失業率升至5.2%。電子設備產出卻增逾19%，顯示AI相關生產與疲弱整體經濟分化。政策銀行債指數週一上漲0.08%，與已開發市場長債不同。本地需求仍重要，但中國疲弱尚未抵銷其他能源進口國面對的限制。

## 印度流動性意外收縮，希臘則以還債減少供給

印度央行將在8月底關閉海外居民美元存款特殊窗口，比原定早一個月，儘管總裁Sanjay Malhotra在8月5日會議曾排除提前結束。5年期印債殖利率最多升9個基點至6.44%，10年期則升4個基點至6.80%。較少存款意味未來盧比流動性減少，影響因此較集中在曲線前端。

窗口已吸引逾$500億，協助外匯存底三週增加超過$300億至$7,070億。花旗將總流入預測下修$100億至$700億，並預期盧比升值空間止於每美元95附近；週一盧比貶0.2%至95.58。央行似乎在權衡，更多準備資產與其承擔的三至五年外債、遠期溢價成本是否仍划算。

國營企業與銀行的其他窗口仍開放至12月，境外借款優惠換匯提供固定年率1.5%，要求平均到期至少三年。印度金融機構今年美元發債創$80億紀錄，超過2019年全年的$79.2億。ICICI週一正行銷，Kotak Mahindra與Yes Bank已委任顧問，評估指標規模發行。強勁訂單支持低於初始利差的定價，但恢復一般避險成本後，渠道吸引力可能下降。

希臘則以盈餘降低未來供給。計畫2026年提前償還約€130億，包括約€25億歐洲金融穩定機制貸款，以及2027年到期的€22億債券，12月31日前國庫券餘額另減€12億。方案尚未定案，6月已先償還€69億紓困貸款。

希臘預期初級盈餘再次超標，債務占GDP降至137%，低於先前預測138.2%，年底現金超過€300億。比率更快下降，可能使義大利在年底前成為歐洲債務占GDP最高的國家，早於歐盟執委會原估的明年。提前償還2027年券可降低未來需求，使明年融資策略與今年相近。希臘10年期殖利率已低於義大利、法國與英國，顯示全球利率上升之際，可信的供給減少仍有價值。

新興市場抗通膨債也有不同表現。規模$8,860億的市場截至週五報酬11.1%，相較廣泛本地債1.6%、全球綜合指數負0.2%。匯率升值助益明顯，尤其拉丁美洲；哥倫比亞披索、巴西雷亞爾與墨西哥披索，是今年三個最強新興貨幣。漲幅累積後，巴西隱含通膨偏貴，長期名目殖利率已達約15%的水準。波蘭較便宜，部分因大量供給缺乏巴西那樣的退休基金自然需求；智利與哥倫比亞估值較均衡。

土耳其通膨預測由26%上修至28%，阿根廷、印度、南非與羅馬尼亞通膨高於預期，巴西及哥倫比亞也仍具黏性，讓通膨保護保持相關性。聖嬰可能增加拉美食品與電力成本，但過去抗通膨債的報酬，不能抹平供給、買方結構、實質殖利率及匯率曝險差異。

## 巴西高利率壓力傳入企業，重整期限迫近

巴西6月活動指數下降0.64%，差於預期0.5%，為2025年5月以來最大跌幅。第二季仍成長0.2%、年增2.35%，但第一季財政支持後，利率敏感部門開始疲弱。8月連續第四次降息25個基點，Selic仍為14%，通膨高於3%目標，9月須視數據決定。

財長Dario Durigan承認，市場對強制性支出及公債的疑慮有道理。雷亞爾前一週連跌五個交易日，隨魯拉選舉領先擴大，外資截至8月12日從股市撤出逾BRL135億、約$26億。通膨預期至2028年仍高於目標。Durigan稱財政是政府降低結構性高利率的主要工具，卻未支持調整退休金指數化或支出規則，具體措施仍缺席。

Casas Bahia在2024年庭外重整未能恢復流動性後，進入法院監督的破產保護。公司列出高利率、信用收緊、消費弱與營運資金壓力，負債達BRL173億。上半年淨營收BRL144億，淨損BRL112億、較去年擴大18.4%。已關閉298家門市，計畫維持其餘營運並延展債務。法院保護提供處理程序，不等於獲利或債權價值恢復。

Petrobras考慮延長Braskem付款期限、降低利息並增加輕油供應。早先較嚴條件使其占Braskem原料比重，由最高70%降至約30%，提高銀行借款需求。商業條件放寬可減少營運資金債務，但尚無決定或時程。Braskem須在8月24日前取得至少三分之一債權支持，才能以庭外方案避免司法重整。

Braskem股票曾為BRL210億未償銀行貸款作擔保，貸款後來售予IG4管理基金，後者目前共同掌控公司。Elliott與Contrarian等債券持有人，希望Petrobras提供股本、營運資金或次順位債。Petrobras抗拒增資，因持股增加可能須合併認列Braskem債務。較好商業條件可改善現金，仍未解決股東與債權人如何分攤損失及新資金。

印尼Modernland Realty也面臨8月24日表決。公司提議將$2.745億債券由2027年4月延至2028年6月，最終換成永續證券，以債權人控制載體中的資產支持。持有人每$1,000本金先收$50，累積3%PIK利息，未付息併入本金；部分擔保品釋出，用於新的$3,400萬融資。新流動性伴隨擔保改變、現金利息延後及更長回收期，不只是其他條件不變的展期。

## 接下來看Fed溝通、20年期標售與實際油流

8月19日7月FOMC會議紀錄，以及Warsh傑克森洞發言，將說明官員如何衡量轉弱的就業、物價與零售。7月以9比3維持利率，目前市場已將下次升息放到1月。若討論比票數顯示更接近升息，或強調逾55%核心商品仍漲價，2年期可能更深入跌勢；若支持耐心，調整就較多留在長端實質殖利率與供給補償。

$160億20年期標售將直接檢驗最新讓利後的長債需求。30年期殖利率升至5.31%時，20年以上現券成交週一增加15.1%至原始面額$1,344億。得標接近當時發行前利率、後續交易穩定，表示買方回應價格；若明顯偏高得標或曲線再陡，則顯示紀錄性公司發行及海外供給，仍壓過Fed路徑較溫和的利多。

替代原油轉運、恢復通航及較低運費或保險成本，有助限制布蘭特升至$91.12的壓力。若替代油流失敗、攻擊再起或伊朗港口執法加強，衝擊就可能擴至通膨補償與政策定價。損益兩平通膨率與2年期殖利率是否更緊跟油價，將區分這種情境與持續由實質殖利率主導的曲線轉陡。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Long Treasury yields reach new highs as AI borrowers compete for capital

## A later Fed hike does not protect the long bond

The 30-year Treasury yield rose 6 basis points to 5.31%, its highest since 2007, even as traders pushed the expected next Fed increase into January. Ten-year yields gained 4 basis points to 4.72%, while two- and five-year yields rose 2 to 4.19% and 4.38%. The curve steepened again: 2s10s widened 2 basis points to 53, and 2s30s 4 to 112.

Oil added pressure after the June US-Iran memorandum expired without a lasting agreement and Trump said he was not interested in extending it. WTI gained 3.05% to $84.91 and Brent 2.94% to $91.12. But ten-year breakevens rose only 1 basis point to 2.28%, against a 3-basis-point increase in real yields to 2.44%. The larger move was in the return demanded after inflation, as public borrowing and AI investment competed for long-term savings.

August investment-grade issuance reached a record $145.2 billion. Blackstone Private Credit Fund and Blue Owl Technology Finance enlarged deals, while Alphabet began marketing in Australian dollars. Investors continued to finance borrowers, but longer-duration assets suffered: LQD fell 0.40%, HYG and JNK about 0.13% each, and a US government index beyond 20 years lost 0.77%. Sammons Financial provided a separate, issuer-specific shock as related-party concerns drove its spreads wider.

The closing risk picture remained uneven: S&P 500 fell 0.52%, Nasdaq 100 0.17%, but semiconductors gained 1.64%. The Dollar Index declined 0.13% to 99.54 and gold futures rose 2.25% to $4,479.10. AI earnings optimism and a later expected Fed hike coexisted with more expensive long-term capital rather than shielding every asset from it.

Overseas, weak Japanese GDP did not prevent ten-year JGB yields reaching 2.93%, the highest since 1996. India unexpectedly shortened a dollar-deposit facility, reducing anticipated rupee liquidity and hitting shorter bonds. Greece instead planned early repayment to cut future supply. The decisions differed, but none justified assuming foreign bonds would rally simply because the Fed could wait longer.

## Corporate duration replaces some of the Treasury supply relief

The long bond finished above the previous week's 5.216% auction yield, and the ten-year above its own 4.683% stop. Adequate auction demand had not set a lasting ceiling. Over a month, the two-year yield is just 1 basis point higher, versus 17 at ten years and 25 at 30 years. The 30-year real yield rose 6 basis points Monday to 3.06%, matching the nominal move, while the next quarter-point Fed increase moved to January from December a week earlier.

The borrowing arithmetic helps explain why lower Treasury issuance alone has not relieved duration. With annual federal deficits near $2 trillion and more reliance on bills, ten- and 30-year auction sizes have stayed steady. Barclays estimated net note and bond supply to private investors at about $1.2 trillion this year, $440 billion below 2025. Net corporate supply, however, is expected to rise $474 billion, largely from technology. Less government duration is being offset by another source of debt.

Investment-grade issuance is nearly $1.5 trillion this year, 36% higher than a year earlier. The largest technology companies have borrowed roughly $200 billion, about 25% of Treasury's net note and bond issuance to private investors and five times their 2025 proportion. Bonds beyond ten years account for about 20% of the high-grade calendar, up from 13% last year. The additional $190 billion of long corporate debt is nearly 70% of the $276 billion annual supply of 30-year Treasuries.

Comparable duration with a higher yield can draw funds away from government bonds. Alphabet's recent 30-year paper yielded nearly 6.4%, about 115 basis points over Treasuries, while a Meta-linked data-center bond yielded more than 7.5%. Morningstar data showed US investment-grade bond funds raising corporate allocations to a three-year high of 30% while cutting Treasury holdings. Bank of America economists estimated that heavier corporate and mortgage-backed issuance added about 30 basis points to ten-year yields this year. That is an estimate, not a measured attribution of Monday's move, but it aligns with the change in supply and allocations.

The $145.2 billion August total exceeded the prior record of $136 billion in 2020. Year-to-date issuance of $1.46 trillion was also 8.5% ahead of the comparable point in that record year. Alphabet's $25 billion US deal led the month and was 2026's eighth transaction of at least that size, all by technology issuers. JPMorgan's roughly 20% increase in its TMT forecast to $540 billion provides context for the remaining calendar, which normally accelerates after Labor Day.

Alphabet is now marketing a debut Australian-dollar deal across four maturities, including 20 years, targeting about A$5 billion, or $3.6 billion. It has already issued in dollars, Swiss francs, sterling, euros, Canadian dollars and yen, and last month lifted its 2026 capital-spending forecast to as much as $205 billion. Record offshore-borrower activity in Australia and limited domestic technology exposure may help demand. The company is nevertheless drawing on another savings pool rather than keeping the funding need within US credit.

Oil is a separate risk, not the whole explanation for higher real yields. Covert transfers have allowed Middle Eastern producers to move substantial crude into the Gulf of Oman despite vessel attacks, tempering the shock relative to a complete interruption. Those flows coexist with renewed fighting in Lebanon, the expired memorandum and a US naval blockade with no stated resolution timetable. Their failure would put more pressure on inflation compensation than Monday's small breakeven rise suggests.

## Private-credit borrowers upsize, while insurer concerns widen spreads

Blackstone Private Credit Fund sold $750 million of five-year notes after initially seeking about $500 million, with peak orders near $2 billion. Blue Owl Technology Finance added $400 million to a June issue, twice its minimum target, after demand reached about $1.05 billion. Blue Owl priced at 250 basis points over Treasuries, inside the 265-basis-point spread on the existing bonds. Blackstone cleared at 205, about 25 basis points tighter than initial discussion.

Second-quarter results had eased some earlier concerns about software exposure and redemption limits at parts of private credit. Monday's transactions showed access at investment-grade terms, although the previous week's 36% average order attrition remains a reminder that initial books can shrink when pricing tightens. Strong demand and price discipline are not mutually exclusive.

QTS's Microsoft-linked Project Odyssey in Georgia may grow to $3.9 billion after demand exceeded $8 billion. The five-year bonds are expected to be investment grade, yet a high-6% coupon and discounted price would produce a low-to-mid-7% yield, comparable with single-B debt. Leases and the Microsoft link help the structure, while investors still require compensation for construction, project and tenant concentration. An April QTS deal raised $4.6 billion for Microsoft capacity with $12.5 billion of peak demand. The current marketing terms remain prospective, not a completed sale.

Sammons Financial's June 2036 bonds widened to about 200 basis points over the benchmark from 147 a week earlier, their weakest since issuance. A report focused on ties to Guggenheim Partners, citing filings describing Sammons as a related party and acknowledging incentives that could create conflicts. Hunterbrook Media disclosed that its investment affiliate was short the bonds. Fitch had assigned A- in June, citing very strong capital alongside modestly elevated risk assets.

Sammons had been Guggenheim's largest shareholder, while Guggenheim managed tens of billions for the insurer. US prosecutors and regulators are examining loans from insurers connected to Mark Walter to other parts of his business empire. Guggenheim's first-lien term loan due November 2031 was quoted below 80 cents Monday, from about par on July 20. The scrutiny and price declines bring ownership, control and related-party lending into focus; they do not establish the allegations as proven misconduct.

## Japan's weak GDP meets a currency constraint

Japan grew 1.1% annualized in the second quarter, below a 2% consensus and a revised 1.9% first-quarter pace. It was the third consecutive expansion, but private consumption was flat against an expected 0.4% gain. Capital investment fell 1.2% on a non-annualized basis after a revised 1% decline, rather than rising the forecast 0.5%. Domestic demand alone offered little reason to rush tightening.

JGBs nevertheless sold off. The ten-year yield rose as much as 5.5 basis points to 2.93%, the 20-year 6.5 to 3.815%, and the 30-year 6 to 4.07%, close to May's record. Overnight swaps put a September 18 increase at about 80%. Weak output may temper expectations for consecutive hikes without removing the case for the next one.

The yen traded near 159 per dollar, far weaker than its ten-year average of 126.09 and only partly recovered from July's four-decade low of 163.99. End-July coordinated intervention slowed the decline but did not remove the interest-rate gap. Takaichi's government supports a near-term increase, likely in September or October, and Ueda highlighted upside inflation risks after July's hold at 1%. Currency stabilization is taking a larger role in the argument for tightening.

Former senior currency official Takehiko Nakao advocated increases at every meeting and a rate above 2%, saying 2.25% or 2.5% would not be unusual with inflation around 2%. He cited the rate gap and Japan's $1.2 trillion of reserves as continued intervention capacity. He is not a current policymaker; the comments broaden the public debate rather than establish an official path.

July corporate-goods inflation of 7.2% continues to pressure firms to pass through fuel and material costs. With Hormuz effectively closed, the US supplied almost a third of Japan's June oil imports, against 7% in February. Annual wage gains and utility subsidies may support consumption, but households with fewer wage and asset gains remain exposed to living costs. Takaichi has capped utilities and plans a food sales-tax reduction to 1% for two years from April without a clear funding source, against public debt exceeding twice annual output.

The wider bond market is also far from synchronized easing. Two-thirds of 32 swap markets price increases, with about 400 basis points of tightening across seven major markets over the next year. Korea leads with more than 100 basis points; its government bonds are down nearly 9% this year in local currency and Japan's about 4%. France's ten-year recently reached its highest since 2009, while German and Italian yields are up more than 30 basis points this year.

China provides the contrast. July industrial production growth slowed to 4.5%, retail-sales growth to 0.6%, fixed-asset investment fell 6.7% over the first seven months and urban unemployment rose to 5.2%. Electronic-equipment output grew more than 19%, separating AI-linked production from the weak broader economy. A policy-bank bond index gained 0.08% Monday, unlike developed-market duration. Local demand still matters, but Chinese weakness has not offset the constraints facing other energy importers.

## India's liquidity surprise contrasts with Greek debt retirement

The RBI will close its special dollar-deposit window for overseas residents at end-August, a month early, despite Governor Sanjay Malhotra ruling out that step at the August 5 meeting. India's five-year yield rose as much as 9 basis points to 6.44%, compared with 4 at ten years to 6.80%. Fewer deposits imply less prospective rupee liquidity, concentrating the impact nearer the front of the curve.

The window attracted more than $50 billion and helped reserves rise over $30 billion in three weeks to $707 billion. Citigroup cut its gross-inflow forecast by $10 billion to $70 billion and expected rupee appreciation to be capped near 95 per dollar. The currency weakened 0.2% Monday to 95.58. The RBI appears to have weighed further reserve gains against three- to five-year foreign liabilities and the forward-premium cost it was absorbing.

Separate facilities for state-owned companies and banks stay open through December. The concessional offshore-borrowing swap offers a fixed annual 1.5% rate for average maturity of at least three years. Indian financial institutions have sold a record $8 billion of dollar debt this year, exceeding 2019's full-year $7.92 billion. ICICI was marketing Monday, while Kotak Mahindra and Yes Bank had appointed advisers for possible benchmark sales. Strong books have supported tighter-than-initial pricing, but ordinary hedging costs could eventually make the channel less attractive.

Greece is instead using surpluses to reduce future supply. It plans about €13 billion of early repayment in 2026, including roughly €2.5 billion of European Financial Stability Mechanism loans and a €2.2 billion bond due in 2027. Bills outstanding would fall €1.2 billion by December 31. The plan is not final and follows €6.9 billion of bailout-loan repayment in June.

Greece expects another above-target primary surplus, debt/GDP of 137% rather than the prior 138.2% forecast, and year-end cash above €30 billion. The faster decline could leave Italy with Europe's highest debt burden relative to GDP by year-end, ahead of the European Commission's expectation of next year. Retiring the 2027 bond would allow a funding strategy similar to this year's with fewer future needs. Its ten-year yield has moved below Italy, France and the UK, demonstrating the value of credible supply reduction amid higher global yields.

Inflation-linked EM debt has also differentiated itself. The $886 billion sector returned 11.1% through Friday, versus 1.6% for broader local debt and a 0.2% loss in the global aggregate. Currency gains helped, especially in Latin America: the Colombian peso, Brazilian real and Mexican peso were the year's three strongest EM currencies. After those gains, Brazilian implied inflation looks expensive and long nominal yields reach the mid-teens. Poland looks cheaper partly because heavy issuance lacks Brazil's natural pension demand; Chile and Colombia offer more balanced valuations.

Turkey's forecast increase to 28% from 26%, upside inflation surprises in Argentina, India, South Africa and Romania, and sticky readings in Brazil and Colombia keep inflation protection relevant. El Nino could add Latin American food and electricity costs. But past linker returns do not eliminate differences in issuance, buyer bases, real yields or currency exposure.

## Brazil's rate burden reaches borrowers; restructuring deadlines approach

Brazil's activity index fell 0.64% in June, worse than the 0.5% expected and the largest decline since May 2025. Second-quarter growth was still 0.2%, or 2.35% over a year, but rate-sensitive sectors weakened after the first quarter's fiscal support. August's fourth consecutive 25-basis-point Selic cut left the rate at 14%, with inflation still above the 3% target and September dependent on data.

Finance Minister Dario Durigan acknowledged justified concern about mandatory spending and public debt. The real had fallen for five consecutive sessions the previous week, and foreign equity investors withdrew more than BRL13.5 billion, or $2.6 billion, through August 12 as Lula's election lead strengthened. Inflation expectations remain above target through 2028. Durigan called fiscal policy the government's main lever for reducing structurally high rates, but did not endorse changes to pension indexation or spending rules. A specific adjustment remains absent.

Casas Bahia entered court-supervised bankruptcy protection after its 2024 out-of-court restructuring failed to restore liquidity. It cited high rates, tighter credit, weak consumption and working-capital pressure, with BRL17.3 billion of liabilities. First-half net revenue was BRL14.4 billion and the net loss BRL11.2 billion, 18.4% wider than a year earlier. It closed 298 stores and plans to keep remaining operations running while extending maturities. Court protection provides a process, not a recovery in earnings or creditor value.

Petrobras is considering longer payment terms, lower interest and more naphtha supply for Braskem. Earlier tighter terms reduced its share of Braskem's feedstock from as much as 70% to about 30%, increasing reliance on bank borrowing. Commercial relief could reduce working-capital debt, but no decision or timing is set. Braskem needs support from holders of at least a third of its debt by August 24 for an out-of-court solution that avoids judicial recovery.

Braskem shares had secured BRL21 billion of unpaid bank loans later sold to an IG4-managed fund, which now shares control. Bondholders including Elliott and Contrarian want Petrobras to contribute equity, working capital or junior debt. Petrobras has resisted equity because a larger stake could require consolidation of Braskem debt. Better trade terms may help cash without resolving the division of losses and new capital among shareholders and creditors.

Indonesia's Modernland Realty faces its own August 24 vote. It proposes extending a $274.5 million bond from April 2027 to June 2028, eventually exchanging it for perpetual securities backed by assets in a creditor-controlled vehicle. Holders would receive $50 per $1,000 upfront, accrue 3% PIK interest and capitalize unpaid interest. Some collateral would be released for a new $34 million facility. The proposed liquidity comes with altered security, delayed cash interest and a longer recovery horizon, not merely an extension of an otherwise unchanged bond.

## Fed communication, the 20-year sale and physical oil flows

July FOMC minutes on August 19 and Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks will explain how officials weigh softer jobs, prices and retail sales. July's hold passed 9–3, and market pricing now places the next increase in January. A closer debate than the vote suggests, or emphasis on more than 55% of core goods prices still rising, could bring the two-year further into the selloff. Patience would leave more of the adjustment in long real yields and supply compensation.

The $16 billion 20-year auction will directly test duration demand after the latest concession. Cash trading beyond 20 years rose 15.1% Monday to $134.4 billion in original-face value as the 30-year yield reached 5.31%. An award close to the prevailing when-issued yield and stable secondary trading would show buyers responding to price. A tail or renewed steepening would suggest record corporate issuance and overseas supply still outweigh the less threatening Fed path.

Alternative crude transfers, restored vessel passage and cheaper freight or insurance could contain the pressure that brought Brent to $91.12. Failed alternative flows, renewed attacks or tighter enforcement around Iranian ports would broaden the shock into inflation compensation and policy pricing. Whether breakevens and two-year yields begin to move more closely with oil will distinguish that outcome from continued real-yield-led steepening.
